issues.legal_issue: A final and effective scheme under the housing statute is not a prerequisite to acquisition unless the notification identifies the acquisition as being for execution of a formal scheme prepared under that statute.
material_facts: The land was being acquired for the Housing Board, but the notifications did not state that it was for execution of a scheme prepared by the Board under the housing statute.
No final and effective scheme had been completed when the notifications were issued; the schemes were initiated earlier and finalized later.
The housing statute empowered the Board to execute schemes transferred by the Government or a local authority, as well as schemes prepared under its own scheme-making provisions.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a final and effective scheme did not invalidate these notifications. The scheme requirement identified in the earlier decision applies when a notification expressly states that the land is being acquired to execute a formal scheme prepared by the Housing Board under the housing statute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act does not expressly or by necessary implication require a final scheme before acquisition. Sections 35(2), 35(3), 36 and 70 of the Tamil Nadu Housing Board Act provide for Board functions and acquisitions beyond schemes prepared under sections 37 to 56. The Court distinguished State of Tamil Nadu v. A. Mohammed Yousef, limiting its scheme requirement to acquisition expressly for execution of a scheme prepared under Chapter VII. Arnold Rodricks v. State of Maharashtra and Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi support the principle that acquisition may precede development or preparation of a development plan; Patna Improvement Trust v. Smt. Lakshmi Devi was also relied on.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated a proceeding to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.acquisition_for_housing_authority: The land was intended for a housing authority's use.
predicates.notification_identifies_formal_authority: The acquisition notice expressly stated that the land was needed to execute a formal scheme prepared by the housing authority under its governing statute.
predicates.prior_final_scheme_not_required: A completed formal scheme need not exist before the acquisition notice is issued.

issues.definition: When land is acquired for a housing authority and the notice does not identify execution of its formal statutory scheme as the purpose, a final scheme need not precede the notice.

issues.legal_issue: A public purpose described in general housing and neighbourhood-development terms is not vague when the acquisition concerns a large area.
material_facts: The notifications described the purposes as implementing housing schemes, creating a new neighbourhood, and increasing housing accommodation for neighbourhood development.
The three notifications concerned approximately 400 acres in total; one covered about 97 acres affecting approximately 25 owners.
The notifications did not specify the eventual use of each individual parcel.
issues.conclusion: The public purpose stated in the notifications was not vague in the circumstances; the Government was not required to specify the use to which every parcel would be put.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 5-A of the Land Acquisition Act require sufficient specification to enable a meaningful objection, but whether a purpose is vague depends on the facts and circumstances. A public purpose may be described by reference to the acquisition as a whole where a large area is involved. The Court relied on Arnold Rodricks v. State of Maharashtra, Babu Barkya Thakur v. State of Bombay, Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi and Lila Ram v. Union of India. It read Munshi Singh v. Union of India subject to the explanation in Aflatoon.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated a proceeding to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.broad_housing_development_purpose_stated: The acquisition notice identified housing, neighbourhood creation, or related development as its purpose.
predicates.large_area_acquired: The acquisition covered a substantial area comprising land belonging to multiple owners.
predicates.public_purpose_description_not_vague: The stated purpose is sufficiently particularized and is not legally vague.

issues.definition: Where a large area is acquired and the notice identifies a housing or neighbourhood-development purpose, the description is not vague merely because it does not specify the use of each parcel.

issues.legal_issue: A land-acquisition challenge raised only years after the declaration, when the award is imminent or made, may be rejected for laches if the claimant did not object or act at the appropriate time.
material_facts: The landowners did not file objections in the statutory inquiry or raise the challenged grounds before the declarations were made.
The declarations were made in 1978, but the writ petitions were filed in 1982 or 1983, when awards were about to be made or had already been made.
The challenge included grounds that could have been raised earlier, including the alleged vagueness of the public purpose and procedural defects.
issues.conclusion: The delayed challenges could not be entertained on the grounds available earlier; the delay and laches were fatal to those claims.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant who remains inactive after a declaration and challenges the acquisition only near completion of the proceedings may be barred by laches, particularly where the ground was available earlier. The Court relied on Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi and its discussion of Tilokchand Motichand v. H.B. Munshi and Rabindranath Bose v. Union of India.

predicates.land_acquisition_writ_challenge: A claimant sought judicial review of a land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.challenge_filed_years_after_declaration: The claimant brought the challenge years after the formal declaration and near the award stage.
predicates.no_timely_objection_or_challenge: The claimant did not raise the relevant objection or challenge at an earlier appropriate stage.
predicates.late_acquisition_challenge_barred_by_lac: The court will not entertain the delayed challenge on grounds that were available earlier.

issues.definition: A claimant who brings an acquisition challenge years after the declaration, without having objected or challenged it earlier, may be prevented from pursuing those grounds.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in making an award after the declaration does not invalidate the acquisition on the facts where statutory compensation addresses the delay and the claimants themselves delayed seeking relief.
material_facts: Awards were made in 1983 after declarations made in 1978, and the Court accepted that there had been delay.
The State provision allowed compensation for damage caused when an award was not made within two years, unless the owner materially caused the delay.
The proceedings were pending on the date that made the additional amount under the central statute available, and the claimants had delayed bringing their petitions.
issues.conclusion: The delay in making the awards was not fatal to the acquisition proceedings in these cases, although acquisition proceedings must be concluded without avoidable delay and cannot be delayed indefinitely.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48-A of the Land Acquisition Act, as added by the State legislature, provides compensation for damage caused by delay in making an award beyond two years, subject to the owner's responsibility for the delay. Section 23(1-A) provides an additional amount during the specified period of acquisition proceedings. These provisions informed the result in the circumstances, but do not permit indefinite delay. The Court relied on Ram Chand v. Union of India for the obligation to exercise acquisition powers reasonably and fairly.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and award_delayed_after_declaration and statutory_delay_compensation_available and claimant_delayed_seeking_relief

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated a proceeding to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.award_delayed_after_declaration: The award was made after a substantial interval following the formal declaration.
predicates.statutory_delay_compensation_available: The governing law provided compensation or an additional amount addressing loss associated with the acquisition delay.
predicates.claimant_delayed_seeking_relief: The claimant waited an unreasonable period before seeking judicial relief.
predicates.award_delay_not_fatal: The delay in making the award does not invalidate the acquisition in the circumstances.

issues.definition: When an award is delayed, statutory compensation addresses the delay, and the claimant also delayed seeking relief, the delay need not invalidate the acquisition, though proceedings must still be concluded with reasonable expedition.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who waits years after the acquisition declaration cannot raise a procedural objection to the statutory inquiry for the first time when the award is imminent or has been made.
material_facts: The High Court had found non-compliance with rules requiring notice of the objection hearing to the department and an opportunity for the department to answer objections.
The claimants raised that procedural ground only in writ petitions filed years after the declarations, when awards were imminent or had been made.
The claimants had not raised the ground at the appropriate time.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to decide the merits of the alleged non-compliance because of the claimants' delay and held that they could not raise the contention at that late stage.
issues.legal_principle: A procedural objection to an acquisition inquiry may be rejected where the claimant remains silent for years and raises it only when the proceedings are nearing completion. The Court relied on the principles of laches applied in Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi.

predicates.land_acquisition_writ_challenge: A claimant sought judicial review of a land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.alleged_inquiry_hearing_noncompliance: The claimant alleged that a required participant was not notified of the objection hearing or given an opportunity to respond.
predicates.challenge_filed_years_after_declaration: The claimant brought the challenge years after the formal declaration and near the award stage.
predicates.late_procedural_objection_not_entertaine: The court declines to consider the procedural objection because it was raised too late.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenges inquiry-hearing procedure only years after the declaration and near the award stage, the court may decline to consider the objection without deciding its merits.
